items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: When I joined Duke Ellington in the Cotton Club, it was Arthur Whetsol... and we had...

ctx.x: So did you and Duke get to be friends at the Howard Theatre?

We got to be friends at the Howard Theatre -- not too much, but he knew about me, you know? He had heard about me when I played in the pit band. So when he sent for me, I was just very happy to go over. Whetsol Wetzel was a trumpet player that talked to Duke -- you know Harry Wetzel? Whetsol? No, Arthur Whetsol, the trumpet player, that talked to Duke, to send for me, you know? So I went over, and I started at the Cotton Club.
How long after you met Duke at the Howard was it before he sent for you? Do you remember?

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: Arthur Whetsel called up and said that Duke would like to have Juan in the band. And that's when Juan joined the band.

ctx.x: He was working with Cliff Jackson, in Newark, and his first date with Duke wasn't a record date; it was a broadcast, and Ted Heusen was the announcer, and somebody in the band, I don't know who it was, was sick or out or quit, I don't know which it was -- and he asked for Juan, if he would come up and play that broadcast for him.

And he told Juan he'd be sending for him, and he sent for him to make a record date with him, and he told Juan that he liked him and he would be sending for him. Afterwards, he left New York and went back home to Washington D.C., and Arthur Whetsel called up and said that Duke would like to have Juan in the band.
And that's when Juan joined the band.
